speaker: vo
text: The painter gave up in the end. Painted him about to laugh. That's how I remember him. About to.

speaker: vo
text: Twelve years a fire-warden in the lower wards. You learn to read a fire the way clerks read a ledger. Where it started. How fast. Who wanted it.

speaker: vo
text: Corwen's Wharf burned on a calm night.

speaker: vo
text: No wind. No lightning. Fires don't start themselves on calm nights. This one started in three places at once.

speaker: vo
text: Aurel was inside. Doing the inventory the owner asked him to do. On a Sunday night.

speaker: vo
text: It was insured for twice what it was worth. The magistrate called it an accident. Took him a week.

speaker: vo
text: The owner bought a house in the hills that autumn. I went to his party once. I wasn't invited.

speaker: vo
text: The Quiet Office found me the week they closed the case. Officially, we're crown auditors. Ledgers. Seals. Tariffs. Unofficially, we read the numbers nobody wants read.

speaker: vo
text: The lantern is the Office's. It shows what magic leaves behind. In this city, magic is something you do quietly, or not at all.

speaker: vo
text: Half this city belongs to the Ahm now. The other half owes them. Their master laughs a lot. Men who laugh a lot have usually bought the room.

speaker: vo
text: Tyr watches from the hill. The city watches everyone else. Especially anyone with pointed ears.

speaker: vo
text: Brann thinks every case is about money. He's usually right. Pell draws everything. Even me, when he thinks I'm not looking.

speaker: vo
text: Lately the numbers have started leaving bodies.
